import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a custom order for customer age groups for better visualization
# Ensure all possible age groups are included, even if not present in current sample
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Calculate total sales by product and customer age group
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().unstack()

# Plotting the stacked bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Use the plot method on the grouped DataFrame directly for a stacked bar chart
sales_by_product_age.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, colormap='viridis', ax=plt.gca())

plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left') # Place legend outside the plot
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout() # Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
